subject: Minimum guarantee & excess usage options for Acme Health integration
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Jacobs <tom.jacobs@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Minimum guarantee & excess usage options for Acme Health integration

Tom / Acme procurement team —

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together two practical commercial structures for the hosted API usage for your integration with our ChatAssist model. Attached: pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx and a draft SOW (SOW_draft_v1.pdf) to show implementation milestones.

High-level summary (monthly billing, per-token):
- Option A — Low Floor, Premium Overage (Flexible Floor)
  - Minimum monthly guarantee: $8,000 (equivalent to ~80M tokens at our standard list rate)
  - Overage (on-demand above commit): list rate + 45% premium
  - True-up at quarter end, no retrospective credits except for SLA breaches

- Option B — Anchor Commit + Surge Buffer (preferred for steady workloads)
  - Anchor commit: $20,000 / month (~200M tokens) with 18% discount off list per-token
  - Surge buffer: first 25% above commit billed at commit-adjusted rate + 10% (discount-facing overage)
  - Excess above surge: on-demand at list rate + 20%
  - Quarterly true-up with carry-forward credits for underutilization (up to two quarters)

Key negotiable levers: minimum amount, size of surge buffer, and the overage multiplier. We can also add a pilot month (reduced floor with higher overage) if you want to validate traffic patterns before committing.

Next steps: tell me which option you prefer or provide a target minimum you are comfortable with and I’ll work with Finance and Legal to produce SOW v2 and DocuSign-ready terms. Happy to set a 30-min call this week to walk through the math.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW_draft_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Tom Jacobs <tom.jacobs@acmehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 20:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Minimum guarantee & excess usage options for Acme Health integration

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the clear options. A few immediate concerns from procurement and the product team:

- $20k/month anchor is okay long term but too risky for us in the ramp phase. We prefer either a much smaller initial floor or a month-to-month pilot.
- The proposed overage multipliers feel high relative to our expected burstiness. We estimate 30–40% spike windows; billing at list + 20–45% will materially increase our TCO.
- Would prefer a structure where the first 50% over commit is billed at a narrower premium (e.g., +5–10%) and only heavy sustained excess attracts a steeper overage.

Procurement asked whether Redwood can: 1) waive/eliminate the minimum for the first 60 days while keeping a guaranteed committed rate if we convert; or 2) provide a guaranteed cap on monthly effective per-token price so runaway bursts don't push us above an expected ceiling.

Can your team model Option B with a smaller anchor (say $10k) and a 50% surge window at +8%? Also need to see an example invoice/true-up calculation.

Thanks —
Tom Jacobs
Head of Product Integrations | Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Minimum guarantee & excess usage options for Acme Health integration

Kim — looping Aisha (Sales Ops / Finance) for fast modeling. Quick notes from our side before we reply to Tom: 

- Procurement asks are reasonable; we can present a split solution that reduces initial risk and contains downside for Acme while preserving revenue predictability for Redwood.

Proposed commercial menu (we can offer both and let them pick):

Option 1 — Pilot-then-Convert (lower immediate risk)
- Pilot: 60 days, no minimum, billing at list rate + 12% overage for any consumption.
- If converted to commit within 60 days, we credit 50% of pilot spend toward the first month of the commit.
- True-up monthly during pilot to give visibility; no quarterly true-up until commit begins.

Option 2 — Anchored Commit w/ Wide Surge Buffer (recommended for team)
- Anchor: $10k / month (client suggested) with 14% discount off list per-token.
- Surge buffer: 50% of anchor billed at anchor-adjusted rate + 8% (matches Tom's ask).
- Excess above surge: on-demand at list + 18% with monthly true-up and a 2-quarter carry-forward credit for underuse.
- Cap protection: If a single monthly invoice would cause effective per-token spend > 30% above the anchor per-token, we trigger a capped surcharge path where the excess is capped and we open a usage-review call. This gives Acme a bounded worst-case.

Examples (rounded):
- Anchor $10k (~100M tokens at discounted rate)
- If month spike reaches 150M tokens: first 100M at anchor price, next 50M at anchor+8% -> limited exposure
- If month reaches 250M tokens: 100M anchor, next 50M at anchor+8% (surge), remaining 100M at list+18% (excess) but with a monthly cap that prevents invoice from exceeding the equivalent of list+25% effective price for the month (subject to usage review)

Aisha: can you run a sample invoice for the three scenarios (steady, 50% spike, 150% spike) and attach a draft SOW v2 and an updated pricing matrix?

Thanks —
Marissa

Tom —

Thanks for the quick feedback and the clear asks from procurement. We talked it through internally and can offer two concrete paths that address the risk you described. I’ve attached pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx and SOW_draft_v2.pdf. Below is a concise summary and an example invoice calculation so your finance team can validate.

Option A — Pilot-then-Convert (lower short-term risk)
- 60-day pilot: no minimum. Billing at list rate + 12% for any usage.
- If you convert within 60 days, 50% of pilot spend is credited toward the first committed month.
- Monthly reporting and a one-time onboarding credit for usage that exceeds forecast by >200% in the pilot month.

Option B — Anchored Commit with 50% Surge Buffer (recommended)
- Anchor: $10,000 / month (~100M tokens at discounted rate); Discount: 14% off list per-token.
- Surge buffer: 50% of anchor billed at anchor-adjusted rate + 8% (as requested).
- Excess above surge: on-demand billed at list + 18%.
- Monthly true-up. Underutilization credits can be carried forward for up to two quarters.
- Cap protection: any invoice that would lead to an effective per-token price >30% above anchor will be capped and escalated for a usage review — this provides an explicit ceiling for procurement.

Example invoice (month):
- Anchor price (discounted): $10,000 for 100M tokens = $0.0001/token (example number)
- If actual consumption = 150M tokens:
  - 100M at anchor price = $10,000
  - 50M at surge price (anchor+8%) = $5,400
  - Total = $15,400
- If consumption = 250M tokens:
  - 100M anchor = $10,000
  - 50M surge = $5,400
  - 100M excess at list+18% = $13,600
  - Total = $29,000 (capped if exceeds effective ceiling; see cap protection)

We can also do the pilot option first and convert to Option B after 60 days. Legal/Finance are ready to draft an amendment once you pick a path — I can circulate DocuSign-ready SOW and terms.

Next steps: please indicate which option you prefer (Pilot or Anchor) and whether procurement wants the invoice examples run with your internal forecast numbers — if so, send an expected daily/weekly token profile and Aisha will generate a line-level invoice simulation. I can set up a 30-min commercial review call with Marissa + Aisha early next week.

Appreciate it,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132
